blurb.en: Choose the right verb form in a story and write one grammar word in each email gap.
blurb.vi: Chọn đúng dạng động từ trong câu chuyện và điền một từ ngữ pháp vào mỗi chỗ trống trong email.

passive.def: A verb form where the action is done to the subject, like 'is made' or 'was built'.
passive.ex: 'Paper is made from wood' is a *passive* sentence.

present perfect.def: have or has + past participle, for past actions that are linked to now.
present perfect.ex: 'I have finished' is in the *present perfect*.

past simple.def: A verb form for finished actions at a time in the past.
past simple.ex: 'We visited the zoo last Sunday' is in the *past simple*.

first conditional.def: If + present, will + verb: a real possibility in the future.
first conditional.ex: 'If it rains, we will stay inside' is a *first conditional*.

auxiliary.def: A helping verb, like be, have, do or will, that goes with a main verb.
auxiliary.ex: In 'She has gone home', 'has' is the *auxiliary*.

relative pronoun.def: Who, which, whose, where or that: it adds information about a noun.
relative pronoun.ex: In 'the boy who won', 'who' is a *relative pronoun*.

modal.def: A word like must, should, can or needn't that goes before another verb.
modal.ex: 'Should' is a *modal* that we use to give advice.

article.def: The small words a, an and the that go before a noun.

preposition.def: A small word like on, at, by or without that goes before a noun.

gap.def: An empty space in a sentence where a word is missing.

clue.def: A word near the gap that helps you find the answer.
clue.ex: 'Since 2020' is a *clue* that tells you to use the present perfect.

subject.def: The person or thing that does the action, usually before the verb.
subject.ex: In 'Mai plays chess', Mai is the *subject*.

tense.def: The form of a verb that shows past, present or future time.
tense.ex: 'Yesterday' tells you to use a past *tense*.

scenes.head: A short report on the class blog
scenes.html: Our new school bus *was delivered* last week. It *is powered* by electricity, so it is very quiet. The seats *were made* from recycled plastic. Our driver, Mr Tan, *has driven* buses *for* twenty years, and he says it is the best bus he has ever had!

steps.en: *was delivered*, *is powered* and *were made* are passive. The bus didn't do these actions.
steps.vi: *was delivered*, *is powered* và *were made* là bị động. Chiếc xe buýt không tự làm những việc này.

steps.en: Present passive = am / is / are + past participle. Past passive = was / were + past participle.
steps.vi: Bị động hiện tại = am / is / are + quá khứ phân từ. Bị động quá khứ = was / were + quá khứ phân từ.

steps.en: *has driven* ... *for* twenty years is present perfect: it started in the past and is still true now.
steps.vi: *has driven* ... *for* twenty years là thì hiện tại hoàn thành: bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn đúng đến bây giờ.

scenes.head: An email from Lan
scenes.html:
Hi Kenji,
I've *just* joined a kite club. We meet *at* the weekend. Our leader is Mr Ortiz, *who* used to be a pilot. He showed us how *to* fly a stunt kite. *If* it *is* windy on Saturday, we *will* go to the beach. *Would* you like to come?
Lan

steps.en: Part 4 of the exam takes out small grammar words like the ones in gold.
steps.vi: Phần 4 của bài thi bỏ đi những từ ngữ pháp nhỏ giống các từ màu vàng.

steps.en: *who* follows a person (Mr Ortiz). 'how *to* fly' needs *to* before the verb.
steps.vi: *who* đi sau một người (Mr Ortiz). 'how *to* fly' cần *to* trước động từ.

steps.en: *If* it *is* windy ... we *will* go: present after 'if', and 'will' in the other part.
steps.vi: *If* it *is* windy ... we *will* go: dùng hiện tại sau 'if', và 'will' ở vế còn lại.

title.vi: Chọn động từ khuyết thiếu đúng

scenes.head: Notes for the class camping night
scenes.html: You *must* bring a torch. You *needn't* bring a tent: the school has tents for everyone. You *should* pack a warm jumper because nights can be cold. You *mustn't* leave food outside your tent.

steps.en: *must* = it is necessary. *mustn't* = it is not allowed.
*needn't* = it is not necessary. *should* = it is good advice.
steps.vi: *needn't* = không cần thiết. *should* = lời khuyên tốt.

steps.en: Read the whole sentence. The reason after ':' or 'because' tells you which modal fits.
steps.vi: Đọc cả câu. Lí do sau dấu ':' hoặc 'because' cho em biết động từ khuyết thiếu nào phù hợp.

end.en: Brilliant! You chose the right verb forms and grammar words.
end.vi: Tuyệt vời! Em đã chọn đúng dạng động từ và từ ngữ pháp.

challenge.result: You spotted passives, present perfect, relatives and modals!

v.q: Which sentence is passive?
whys: Lan does the action, so this is active.
Lan does the action, so this is active too.
v.hint: Look for was / were + past participle.
v.worked: 'The cake *was eaten*' = was + past participle. We don't say who ate it.

v.q: The first car .......... more than a hundred years ago.
whys: A car can't invent something. Someone invented the car.
'a hundred years ago' is past time, so 'is' is wrong.
v.hint: Did the car do the action, or did someone do it to the car? When?
v.worked: Someone invented the car, long ago: past passive *was invented*.

v.q: So far, I .......... to Ha Long Bay three times.
whys: 'So far' means up to now, so we need the present perfect.
'So far' and 'three times' talk about your life up to now.
v.hint: Find the clue words 'So far'.
v.worked: '*So far*' = up to now, so we use *have been*.

v.q: Has Minh finished his model ..........?
whys: 'already' is not used at the end of a question like this.
'since' needs a time after it, like 'since Monday'.
v.hint: Which word goes at the end of a present perfect question?
v.worked: 'Has he finished it *yet*?' We use *yet* in questions and negatives.

v.q: The woman .......... car is red is my aunt.
whys: 'who car' is wrong. We need a word that shows the car belongs to her.
'which' is for things, and we need a word for belonging.
v.hint: The car belongs to the woman. Which word shows belonging?
v.worked: *whose* shows belonging: the woman *whose* car is red.

v.q: This is the museum .......... we saw the dinosaur.
whys: 'which' would need 'in' at the end: 'which we saw the dinosaur in'.
'who' is for people, not places.
v.hint: The museum is a place. Which word do we use for places?
v.worked: For a place, use *where*: the museum *where* we saw it.

v.q: You .......... bring food: lunch is free.
whys: Food isn't banned. It just isn't necessary.
Lunch is free, so it isn't good advice to bring food.
v.hint: Read the reason after the colon (:).
v.worked: Lunch is free, so bringing food is not necessary: *needn't*.

v.q: We travelled to Hue .......... train.
whys: We say 'on the train', with 'the'. Here there is no 'the'.
We say 'in the car', not 'in train'.
v.hint: Think of 'by bus', 'by car'.
v.worked: For transport with no article we use *by*: *by train*.

blurb.en: Practise one grammar point at a time, then type the missing word.
blurb.vi: Luyện từng điểm ngữ pháp, rồi gõ từ còn thiếu.

v.q: Paper .......... from wood.
whys: Paper can't make anything. Someone makes paper.
'Paper made from wood' has no main verb. We need 'is'.
v.hint: Does paper do the action? If not, use the passive.
v.worked: Someone makes paper, so we use the present passive: *is made*.

v.q: This bridge .......... in 1998.
whys: A bridge can't build. People built it.
1998 is in the past, so 'is' is wrong.
v.hint: Look at the date. Who did the building?
v.worked: People built it in the past: past passive *was built*.

v.q: I .......... my homework, so I can play now.
whys: If you 'finish' every day, it doesn't explain why you can play now.
If you are still finishing it, you can't play yet.
v.hint: The action is done, and the result is now. Which form?
v.worked: Done in the past, result now (I can play): *have finished*.

v.q: My cousin .......... in Da Nang since 2020.
whys: 'since 2020' means it is still true now, so not the past simple.
With 'since' we need the present perfect, not the present simple.
v.hint: Find the clue word 'since'.
v.worked: *since* 2020 up to now: *has lived*.

v.q: If you water the plant every day, it .......... quickly.
whys: 'grew' is past, but this is about the future.
After 'If + present' we use 'will', not 'would'.
v.hint: If + present ... then what?
v.worked: If + present (*water*), then *will* + verb: *will grow*.

v.q: If it .......... tomorrow, we will play inside.
whys: We don't use 'will' after 'if' in this sentence.
'rained' is past, but 'tomorrow' is the future.
v.hint: Which part has 'will'? What form goes after 'if'?
v.worked: After *if* we use the present: If it *rains*, we will play inside.

title.vi: Động từ khuyết thiếu, who / which / whose, giới từ

v.q: You .......... bring a pen. I've got lots of them.
whys: Bringing a pen isn't against the rules.
I have lots of pens, so it isn't necessary.
v.hint: Read the second sentence. Is a pen necessary?
v.worked: I've got lots of pens, so it is not necessary: *needn't*.

v.q: You look tired. You .......... go to bed earlier.
whys: Going to bed earlier is a good idea for a tired person.
Going to bed early isn't against the rules.
v.hint: This is advice. Which modal gives advice?
v.worked: To give advice we use *should*.

v.q: That's the girl .......... brother plays in our team.
whys: 'who brother' is wrong. We need a word that shows belonging.
'which' is for things, not people.
v.hint: The brother belongs to the girl. Which word shows belonging?
v.worked: The girl's brother = the girl *whose* brother.

v.q: Is this the bus .......... goes to the zoo?
whys: 'who' is for people. A bus is a thing.
The bus isn't a place here. It is the thing that goes.
v.hint: Is a bus a person, a thing or a place?
v.worked: A bus is a thing, so we use *which*.

v.q: We always go to school .......... foot.
whys: We say 'by bus', but for walking we say 'on foot'.
'in foot' is not English.
v.hint: Remember the fixed phrase for walking.
v.worked: Walking = *on foot*.

v.q: Sorry! I broke the vase .......... mistake.
whys: 'on purpose' means you wanted to do it. Here it was an accident.
'in mistake' is not English.
v.hint: It was an accident. Which phrase means that?
v.worked: An accident = *by mistake*.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: She {0} just finished her painting.
v.hint: 'just' + finished: which helping verb goes with 'she'?
v.worked: Present perfect: she *has* just finished.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: These shoes {0} made in a small factory last year.
v.hint: 'last year' is past. 'These shoes' is plural.
v.worked: Past passive, plural: these shoes *were* made.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: This is the park {0} we play football every Sunday.
v.hint: The park is a place.
v.worked: For a place we use *where*: the park *where* we play.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: Mr Duc, {0} is our new coach, used to play for the national team.
v.hint: Mr Duc is a person, and there are commas around the extra information.
v.worked: For a person with commas we use *who* (not 'that').

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: I want {0} learn how to code.
v.hint: want + ... + verb
v.worked: We say want *to* + verb: I want *to* learn.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: Please don't leave the classroom {0} permission.
v.hint: You need someone to say yes first. Which word means 'with no'?
v.worked: *without* permission = when nobody has said yes.

title.vi: Phần 1: một câu chuyện, năm câu

v.q:
Story: The fun run (sentence 1 of 5)
Last Saturday, a fun run .......... by our school to raise money for the local hospital.
whys: The fun run didn't organise anything. The school organised it, so use the passive.
'Last Saturday' is finished past time, so we need a past form.
v.hint: Find 'by our school'. Who did the action?
v.worked: The run was organised *by our school*, last Saturday: past passive *was organised*.

v.q:
Story: The new science room (sentence 1 of 5)
Our new science room .......... by the head teacher last month.
whys: The room didn't open anything. The head teacher opened it.
'last month' is finished time, and the room didn't do the action.
v.hint: Find 'by the head teacher' and 'last month'.
v.worked: The head teacher opened it, last month: past passive *was opened*.

v.q:
Story: The fun run (sentence 2 of 5)
On the day, more than two hundred people .......... part, including parents and teachers.
whys: People did the action, so we don't need the passive.
'On the day' is a finished time in the past, so use the past simple.
v.hint: The people did the action. When?
v.worked: Active, finished past time: people *took* part.

v.q:
Story: The new science room (sentence 2 of 5)
The room has smart boards, and all the tables .......... from recycled wood.
whys: Tables can't make anything. Someone made them.
The tables need a full verb here: are + past participle.
v.hint: Did the tables do the action? The text is in the present.
v.worked: Someone makes the tables, and 'has' tells us it is present: *are made*.

v.q:
Story: The fun run (sentence 3 of 5)
Runners .......... wear special running shoes, but everyone had to wear a number.
whys: 'mustn't' is present and means 'not allowed'. Shoes weren't banned.
'don't have to' is present, but the story is in the past ('had to').
v.hint: Read after 'but': 'had to wear a number'. So the shoes were...?
v.worked: Special shoes were not necessary in the past: *didn't have to*.

v.q:
Story: The new science room (sentence 3 of 5)
We .......... any experiments in the new room yet because the microscopes haven't arrived.
whys: 'yet' goes with the present perfect, not the past simple.
'yet' goes with the present perfect, not the present simple.
v.hint: Find the clue word 'yet'.
v.worked: *yet* + not up to now: *haven't done*.

v.q:
Story: The fun run (sentence 4 of 5)
So far, the school .......... enough money to buy two new beds for the hospital.
whys: 'So far' means up to now, so use the present perfect.
The school did the action, so we don't need the passive.
v.hint: Find the clue words 'So far'.
v.worked: '*So far*' = up to now: the school *has raised* the money.

v.q:
Story: The new science room (sentence 4 of 5)
Our teacher says we .......... touch the microscopes without asking her first.
whys: 'needn't' means 'not necessary'. This is a rule about what is not allowed.
'don't have to' means 'not necessary'. This is a rule about what is not allowed.
v.hint: Is it a rule (not allowed) or is it just not necessary?
v.worked: Touching without asking is not allowed: *mustn't*.

v.q:
Story: The fun run (sentence 5 of 5)
If we .......... the same amount next year, the hospital will open a new playroom.
whys: We don't use 'will' after 'if' in the first conditional.
'next year' is the future, so 'raised' is wrong.
v.hint: The other part has 'will'. What goes after 'if'?
v.worked: If + present (*raise*), ... *will* open.

v.q:
Story: The new science room (sentence 5 of 5)
If the microscopes arrive on Monday, we .......... at onion cells on Tuesday.
whys: 'looked' is past, but Tuesday is in the future.
After 'If + present' we use 'will', not 'would'.
v.hint: 'If ... arrive' is present. What goes in the other part?
v.worked: If + present (*arrive*), we *will look*.

v.q: Read the email. Write ONE word for gap 18.
lines: Sorry I haven't written {0} ages!
v.hint: 'ages' is a long time. Which word goes before a length of time?
v.worked: Present perfect + a length of time: *for* ages.

items.en: Passive: *am / is / are* + past participle (now), *was / were* + past participle (past). Use it when the subject doesn't do the action.
items.vi: Bị động: *am / is / are* + quá khứ phân từ (hiện tại), *was / were* + quá khứ phân từ (quá khứ). Dùng khi chủ ngữ không tự làm hành động.
example: Rice *is grown* in the Mekong Delta.

items.en: Present perfect with *just, already, yet, ever, never, for, since, so far*. Past simple with *yesterday, last week, ago, in 2019*.
items.vi: Hiện tại hoàn thành đi với *just, already, yet, ever, never, for, since, so far*. Quá khứ đơn đi với *yesterday, last week, ago, in 2019*.

items.en: First conditional: *If* + present, *will* + verb. Never put 'will' straight after 'if'.
items.vi: Câu điều kiện loại 1: *If* + hiện tại, *will* + động từ. Không đặt 'will' ngay sau 'if'.

items.en: Modals: *must* = necessary, *mustn't* = not allowed, *needn't / don't have to* = not necessary, *should* = advice.
items.vi: Động từ khuyết thiếu: *must* = bắt buộc, *mustn't* = không được phép, *needn't / don't have to* = không cần thiết, *should* = lời khuyên.
example: You *needn't* bring a towel: we have lots.

items.en: Relative pronouns: *who* (people), *which* (things), *whose* (belonging), *where* (places). After a comma, don't use 'that'.
items.vi: Đại từ quan hệ: *who* (người), *which* (vật), *whose* (sở hữu), *where* (nơi chốn). Sau dấu phẩy, không dùng 'that'.
example: That's the boy *whose* dog won the prize.
Hanoi, *which* is my home town, is very busy.

items.en: Part 4 gap words: prepositions with nouns (*by bus, on foot, on time, without permission*), *to* after want / going / looking forward, and *the* before superlatives.
items.vi: Từ hay điền ở Phần 4: giới từ đi với danh từ (*by bus, on foot, on time, without permission*), *to* sau want / going / looking forward, và *the* trước so sánh nhất.

check.sentence: The first bicycles {were made|made|are made} of wood.
I {have lived|lived|live} here since I was five.
If we {leave|will leave|left} now, we will catch the bus.
You {needn't|mustn't|should} take an umbrella: it's sunny all day.
That's the girl {whose|who|which} cat is called Mochi.

v.q:
Story: The bird boxes (sentence 1 of 5)
Last term, our class .......... five bird boxes on the trees around the playground.
whys: Our class did the action, so we don't need the passive.
'Last term' is finished past time, so use the past simple.
v.hint: Who did the action? When?
v.worked: Our class did it, *last term*: past simple active *put up*.

v.q:
Story: The water fountain (sentence 1 of 5)
Last month, a new water fountain .......... in our school playground.
whys: A fountain can't install anything. Someone installed it.
'Last month' is past, and the fountain didn't do the action.
v.hint: Did the fountain do the action? When?
v.worked: Someone installed it *last month*: past passive *was installed*.

v.q:
Story: The bird boxes (sentence 2 of 5)
The boxes .......... from old wooden fruit boxes that a local shop gave us.
whys: The boxes didn't make anything. We made them.
The boxes didn't do the action, and it happened in the past.
v.hint: Did the boxes do the action? Look at 'gave': past or present?
v.worked: We made the boxes in the past: past passive, plural *were made*.

v.q:
Story: The water fountain (sentence 2 of 5)
The water .......... by a special filter, so it is safe to drink.
whys: Water can't clean itself. The filter cleans it.
The sentence is about now ('it is safe'), and it needs 'is'.
v.hint: Find 'by a special filter'. Who does the cleaning?
v.worked: The filter cleans the water, now: present passive *is cleaned*.

v.q:
Story: The bird boxes (sentence 3 of 5)
Since then, two families of birds .......... in them.
whys: 'Since then' means up to now, so not the past simple.
With 'since' we use the present perfect, not the present simple.
v.hint: Find the clue word 'Since'.
v.worked: *Since* then, up to now: *have lived*.

v.q:
Story: The water fountain (sentence 3 of 5)
Since it arrived, most students .......... their own bottles to school every day.
whys: 'Since it arrived' means up to now, so not the past simple.
With 'since' we use the present perfect, not the present simple.
v.hint: Find the clue word 'Since'.
v.worked: *Since* it arrived, up to now: *have brought*.

v.q:
Story: The bird boxes (sentence 4 of 5)
We .......... go too close to the boxes because the birds might get scared.
whys: 'needn't' means 'not necessary'. Here going close is a bad thing that isn't allowed.
'don't have to' means 'not necessary'. Here going close isn't allowed.
v.hint: Read the reason after 'because'. Is it a rule?
v.worked: The birds might get scared, so it is not allowed: *mustn't*.

v.q:
Story: The water fountain (sentence 4 of 5)
Our teacher says we .......... buy drinks at the shop any more, but we can if we want to.
whys: 'we can if we want to' shows it isn't banned.
'any more' needs a negative word, and buying isn't necessary.
v.hint: Read after 'but': 'we can if we want to'.
v.worked: We can if we want, so it is not necessary: *needn't*.

v.q:
Story: The bird boxes (sentence 5 of 5)
If the baby birds .......... this spring, we will take photos from the classroom window.
whys: We don't use 'will' straight after 'if' here.
'this spring' is in the future, so the past is wrong.
v.hint: The other part has 'will'. What goes after 'if'?
v.worked: If + present (*hatch*), we *will* take photos.

v.q:
Story: The water fountain (sentence 5 of 5)
If more students .......... reusable bottles, the school will need fewer bins.
whys: We don't use 'will' straight after 'if' here.
With 'will need' in the other part, we use the present, not the past.
v.hint: The other part has 'will'. What goes after 'if'?
v.worked: If + present (*use*), the school *will* need fewer bins.
